label: SIMULATION — NOT PHYSICAL-SYSTEM VALIDATION

scenario.title: Unauthorized temperature setpoint change
scenario.attempted: An attacker changes the controller setpoint from −22 °C to +2 °C outside the governed route.

submissions.label: Corrective action: restore the authorized baseline

steps.detail: Independent EIN status FAULT; on-call technician and facility manager notified (simulated).
FM-01 issues a fresh, scoped corrective authority to TECH-01.
Controller restored from the sealed authorized configuration (assumes the attacker's access was also removed).

outcome: Baseline restored under fresh authority at minute 285. Simulated product peaked at -18.43 °C and spent 0 min above -18 °C; at the end it was -21.37 °C. Product disposition is not decided by TA-14.

claims.basis: The command bypassed the governed route and changed controller behaviour. AEA cannot prevent a command that never reaches it.
Ground-truth deviation from minute 212; independent EIN flagged a deviation at minute 215 (35 min after the change).
No AEA determination or execution record exists for the bypassed command; the record states the absence instead.
Chain valid: true (593 entries); sealed baseline unchanged: true; missing entry types: none.

unproven: Detection speed for slower or subtler setpoint drift (e.g. −22 → −19 °C) was not examined.
Physical-system behaviour: the thermal model is illustrative and unvalidated.
Real controller protocols, network paths and attacker capabilities were not tested.
Detection depends on independent sensors existing, being installed correctly and staying independent of the compromised path.

baseline.label: SIMULATION — NOT PHYSICAL-SYSTEM VALIDATION
baseline.thresholdBasis: Configured for this simulation. -18 °C is a commonly cited frozen-storage temperature; site limits must come from the operator's food-safety plan and equipment documentation.

payload.note: The last authorized baseline is sealed and stored separately from observed reality.
